answer: Use unpredictable liveness checkpoints as the inlet to reputation: a new identity enters a violet-tinted probationary grove where verifiers issue short, randomly timed challenges over several weeks. Each response must arrive within a narrow window and match a fresh nonce, so one operator cannot shepherd many identities at once. Missed checks freeze quota, and repeated failures burn its bond. An attacker therefore pays continuous attention and device time per fake identity, while an honest user pays only a few brief responses.
